summary: High rate of tied rerank scores when customer mixes legacy (768) and compact (384) embeddings
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a high proportion of exact-score ties coming out of the rerank endpoint after they started sending a mixed mix of legacy 768-dim embeddings and a newer compact 384-dim embedding set. The customer had been gradually migrating; some clients still send legacy vectors and others send compact vectors.

Impact:
- MezzoSearch says ~18% of their rerank responses show multiple items with identical scores, causing nondeterministic top-K ordering and downstream UX flakiness for end users.
- This affects production search for their enterprise customers (SLA-sensitive).

Environment:
- prod-us-east; requests go through api-gateway -> rerank-endpoint (v2) -> embeddings-service for normalization checks.
- Observed across both dedicated and hosted model variants used by customer.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied minimal repro):
1) Create two embeddings for same text using models redwood-embed-legacy-768-v1 and redwood-embed-compact-384-v2.
2) Store both embedding types in the same index (customer uses hybrid index).
3) Issue rerank request with query embedding generated by compact model, include 10 candidate doc embeddings (mix of 768 and 384).
4) Observe rerank response; several docs show identical similarity values (e.g., 0.7423).

Observed behaviour:
- Exact floating-point equality in returned scores for multiple docs (not just rounded ties).
- Ties correlate with candidates where legacy vectors were zero-padded on the client to 768 before upstream storage.
- When requests are served in different batch paths (continuous batching vs single-request path) tie frequency varies — higher during larger batching windows.

Expected behaviour:
- Rerank should preserve ranked diversity and provide stable tie-breaker ordering; mixing incompatible-dimension embeddings should be rejected or normalized consistently.

Relevant logs/snippets (customer provided):
- Sample response scores: [0.74234271, 0.74234271, 0.74199812, ...]
- Customer header: X-Embed-Version: compact_v2 for query, stored docs have metadata embed_version: [legacy_v1, compact_v2, legacy_v1, ...].
- API trace show rerank worker path: batch_id=1324, kernel_path=continuous-batch-quantized, normalizer=fast-l2, fallback=zero-pad-check.

Notes:
- Customer is not intentionally zero-padding; their index migration pipeline left legacy vectors as-is, and an internal enrichment step pads legacy vectors to a fixed dimensionality before storing.
- Ties are not random rounding artifacts; investigation suggests normalization differences across code paths can convert tiny numerical differences to exact equality after truncation/quantization and the server-side tie compare uses stringified token score keys for deduping when batch paths merge results.

2026-03-10 - MezzoSearch (Customer): Provided sample dataset (10k candidates) and confirmed issue increases during peak traffic. Mentioned they recently enabled an index padding step in their ingestion pipeline.

2026-03-11 - Luca Romero (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating mixed-dimension index and padding legacy vectors to 768. Observed exact ties when running continuous-batch-quantized kernel due to a code path that quantizes scores to 1e-6 and then formats with '%.6f' for internal merge keys.

2026-03-11 - Lina Chen (ML Infra): Hypothesis: two issues combined: (1) client-side padding results in effectively orthogonal zero-padding that doesn't change dot-product until quantization step, (2) batching/quantization path truncates floating noise leading to exact equal keys. Suggested server-side validation to reject mismatched dimensions and a tie-breaker that uses secondary metric (L2 distance) deterministically.

2026-03-12 - Luca Romero (SRE): Confirmed hypothesis. Created repro script that runs thousands of rerank batches; tie-rate jumps from ~2% to ~20% when mixing padded 768 and compact 384 vectors. Opened PR to add dimension-validation and to avoid stringifying scores for internal merge keys (see related PRs).

2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha): Update to customer: we're prioritizing a guarded rollback and server-side validation; ETA for hotfix 24h, full regression fix in next deploy window. Asked customer to toggle ingestion padding as temporary mitigation.

2026-03-12 - MezzoSearch (Customer): Temporarily disabled internal padding and saw immediate drop in tie frequency during afternoon test. Asked for recommended permanent solution and whether data reindex is required.

2026-03-12 - Lina Chen (ML Infra): Recommended reindex of legacy vectors with proper dimensionality conversion (compact projection) or store vector metadata and do server-side rejection; provided confluence runbook link for reindexing steps.
investigation_notes:
Summary of root cause: Mixed-dimension embeddings were being coerced into a common storage format via client-side padding. The serving runtime has two scoring paths: a 'fast quantized' batch path and a 'precise' single-request path. The fast path applied a quantization/truncation step and then used stringified truncated scores as merge keys during result aggregation. Tiny floating differences between padded legacy vectors and compact vectors were being truncated to identical string keys, producing exact ties. Secondary tie-breaker logic was weak and nondeterministic across workers.
Actions taken during investigation: reproduced locally with customer sample, measured tie-rate across kernels, traced batch_id->worker mapping, inspected scoring code for format('%.6f') usage, and confirmed quantization bug.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds provided to customer: (1) Disable client-side padding and reindex legacy vectors with recommended compact projection OR mark legacy vectors with explicit metadata so server rejects incompatible dims. (2) Temporary server-side guard deployed: rerank now validates candidate dims vs query dim and rejects mixed-dimension requests with HTTP 400 + informative error. (3) Short-term hotfix removed stringified score merge keys; aggregation now merges by raw float and uses deterministic secondary tie-breaker (L2 distance then doc id).
Planned long-term fixes: add explicit embedding-version header enforcement, console warning for mixed-index detection, and a migration tool to bulk-project legacy vectors. PRs: serving-runtime/pull/2789 (remove string merge keys), serving-runtime/pull/2794 (dimension validation). Console update PR in progress.
Customer acceptance: MezzoSearch verified disabling padding and testing hotfix — tie-rate dropped to <1% in their next run. They requested a reindex guide and offer of engineering assistance.
